contradicting_evidence: A rebound case has tangible support: spot taker-buy shares are approximately 55.5% for BTC and ETH, sampled taker imbalances are positive, and BTC's sampled depth imbalance is strongly positive.

A downside-continuation case also remains credible: only 27 of 100 breadth constituents advance, BTC is down 1.63% over 24h, ETH is down 2.20%, and all observed alt-capitalization buckets have negative average returns.
frozen_forecast.expected_path: A stabilization or modest rebound attempt may continue, but the evidence does not establish its durability or the net 12h direction. BTC has more visible support than ETH; renewed selling remains credible. The small completed-hour gains are not sufficient evidence of recovery.
falsification_conditions: Persistent spot-led BTC and ETH gains accompanied by improving ETH/BTC and broader positive participation would replace the no-edge assessment with an upward case.
Persistent price declines, worsening participation and failure of the current buying interest to support prices would establish a clearer downward case.
missing_evidence: Follow-through after the latest completed hour and persistence of the sampled order-book and taker imbalances.
Whether rising open interest reflects durable demand or leverage vulnerable to reversal.
supporting_evidence: The latest hour shows BTC up 0.071%, ETH up 0.129% and ETH/BTC up 0.068%, contrasting with negative 24h returns rather than establishing a sustained turn.
Final settled ETF flows diverge sharply: BTC +$526.7 million versus ETH -$103.3 million, preventing a uniform demand interpretation.
BTC and ETH both show PRICE_UP_OI_UP, while long/short ratios are 1.84 and 2.46; the small rebound is therefore not demonstrably spot-only.
